lessons.title: I think that

items.english: it seems to me / I feel like

sentences.target: Я думаю, что он на работе.
sentences.translit: Ya dumayu, shto on na rabote.

sentences.english: In my opinion, this is very good.
I feel like it's cold today.
Is that true? No, it's not true!

lines.english: Did you watch the film yesterday?

lessons.tip: "That" = что, and Russian always puts a comma before it: Я думаю, что… Short openers (по-моему, мне кажется) also take a comma after them.

lessons.title: Because & so

sentences.target: Я дома, потому что я устал.
sentences.translit: Ya doma, potomu shto ya ustal.

sentences.english: I feel bad, so I'm home.

sentences.target: Я хочу кофе, но это дорого.
sentences.english: I want coffee, but it's expensive.
sentences.translit: Ya khochu kofe, no eto dorogo.

sentences.target: Если завтра будет дождь, я буду дома.
sentences.english: If it rains tomorrow, I'll be at home.
sentences.translit: Yesli zavtra budet dozhd', ya budu doma.

sentences.english: Although it's cold, I love walking.

sentences.target: Я учу русский, чтобы поехать в Россию.
sentences.english: I'm learning Russian in order to go to Russia.
sentences.translit: Ya uchu russkiy, shtoby poyekhat' v Rossiyu.

fills.english: I'm home because I feel bad.
I feel bad, so I'm home.
I'm learning Russian to talk to people.

lines.target: Ты не хочешь в кино? Ты устал?
lines.english: You don't want to go to the cinema? Are you tired?
lines.translit: Ty ne khochesh' v kino? Ty ustal?

lessons.tip: потому что answers "why" and goes before the reason; поэтому goes before the result. Same two ideas, opposite order: Я дома, потому что я устал. = Я устал, поэтому я дома.

lessons.title: Judging things

sentences.english: The Russian language is hard but interesting.

lessons.tip: Two forms of the same idea. Short, with -о, describes how a thing is going: Это интересно. Long, with an ending, sits next to a noun: интересный фильм, интересная книга.

lessons.title: Dative: I like

sentences.target: Ему нравится футбол, а ей нравится кино.
sentences.english: He likes football, and she likes the cinema.
sentences.translit: Yemu nravitsya futbol, a yey nravitsya kino.

sentences.english: We like walking in the park.
I'm bored at home, and you?

fills.english: He likes football, and she likes the cinema.
I'm having fun at the party.

lines.english: Yes, I like it a lot.

lessons.tip: In Russian you don't "like" — things are pleasing TO you. The person goes into the dative: мне (to me), тебе, ему, ей, нам. The thing you like is the subject: Мне нравится кофе.

lessons.title: Dative: must & may

items.english: I need to / I have to
it's time for me to go

sentences.english: We need to buy a present.
It's time for me to go, I'm tired.
I can't be bothered, and I have no time.

fills.english: It's time for me to go home.
Today I'm working, so I have no time.

lines.english: Shall we go to the cinema?
I can't, I have to work.

lessons.tip: Same dative trick for duty and permission: Мне надо работать, Вам нельзя курить, Им можно играть. Person in the dative + a little word + the verb. Мне пора = it's time for me (to go).

lessons.title: Invitations

items.english: treats / food and drink for guests

sentences.target: Я приглашаю друзей на день рождения.
sentences.english: I'm inviting friends to my birthday.
sentences.translit: Ya priglashayu druzey na den' rozhdeniya.

sentences.english: What should I bring? I'll bring a cake.
Today is a holiday, there will be treats.

fills.english: I'm inviting friends to the party.

lines.english: With pleasure! What should I bring?

lines.target: Ничего не надо, у нас есть угощение.
lines.translit: Nichevo ne nado, u nas yest' ugoshcheniye.

lessons.tip: To tell one person to do something, take the verb and add -и or -й: приходи (come), заходи (drop by), пиши (write). Add -те for вы or a group: приходите.

lessons.title: Meeting up

sentences.english: I'm already here, where are you?
Let's meet in front of the cinema, after work.

fills.english: I'm already here, where are you?

lines.english: By the metro, near the bank.

lessons.tip: Place words like у, возле, около, перед, после, до make the next noun change ending (genitive for most). Don't build it yet. Learn the chunks: у метро, у входа, возле банка, после работы.

lessons.title: Genitive with numbers

sentences.target: У меня два брата и три сестры.
sentences.english: I have two brothers and three sisters.
sentences.translit: U menya dva brata i tri sestry.

sentences.english: There are a lot of people here.
How many people will there be on Saturday?

lines.english: How many people will there be on Saturday?

lessons.tip: Numbers change the noun. After 2, 3, 4 use the genitive singular (два друга, три билета). After 5 and up use the genitive plural (пять рублей, много людей). One counts as normal: один билет.

lessons.title: Нет + genitive

sentences.english: There's no room on the bus.

fills.before: Я хочу есть, но в холодильнике
fills.english: I'm hungry, but there's nothing in the fridge.

lines.english: Shall we go to the cinema?

lines.target: Не могу, у меня нет денег.
lines.english: I can't, I have no money.
lines.translit: Ne mogu, u menya net deneg.

lines.target: Нет проблем, у меня есть билеты.
lines.translit: Net problem, u menya yest' bilety.

lessons.tip: To say something is missing, use нет + genitive: нет времени, нет денег, нет проблем. In the past it's не было, in the future не будет, and the thing stays genitive.

lessons.title: With с

sentences.target: Я иду в кино с другом.
sentences.english: I'm going to the cinema with a friend.
sentences.translit: Ya idu v kino s drugom.

sentences.english: I want to talk with you.
Let's go together, it's boring without you.

sentences.target: С кем ты идёшь в кино?
sentences.english: Who are you going to the cinema with?
sentences.translit: S kem ty idyosh' v kino?

fills.english: I'm going to the cinema with a friend.

lines.target: С кем ты идёшь в кино?
lines.english: Who are you going to the cinema with?
lines.translit: S kem ty idyosh' v kino?

lines.target: А я пойду одна. Пойдёшь со мной?
lines.english: And I'll go alone. Will you come with me?
lines.translit: A ya poydu odna. Poydyosh' so mnoy?

lessons.tip: "With" = с + instrumental: с другом, с семьёй. Pronouns are irregular, so learn them as chunks: со мной, с тобой, с нами, с вами. Before some sounds с becomes со: со мной.

lessons.title: Phone words

sentences.english: A new message on the screen.

fills.english: A new message on the screen.

lessons.tip: Borrowed tech words keep a gender by their ending: смартфон and интернет are he (m), батарея and сеть are she (f), приложение is it (n). Look at the ending and you can guess.

lessons.title: Phone calls

sentences.english: Sorry, I dialled the wrong number.

sentences.target: Плохая связь, мне ничего не слышно.
sentences.english: Bad signal, I can't hear anything.
sentences.translit: Plokhaya svyaz', mne nichevo ne slyshno.

fills.english: Sorry, I dialled the wrong number.
It's busy, I'll call back later.

lines.english: Good afternoon, can I speak to Anna?
Anna's not at home. Call back in the evening.

lessons.tip: Phone talk is made of ready-made lines: Алло? Слушаю. Кто говорит? Можно позвать…? Перезвоните позже. Learn them as blocks. No grammar needed.

lessons.title: Messages

sentences.target: Он не отвечает, он не онлайн.
sentences.english: He isn't answering, he isn't online.
sentences.translit: On ne otvechayet, on ne onlayn.

lines.target: Нет, ничего нет. Скинь ещё раз.
lines.english: No, nothing's here. Send it again.
lines.translit: Net, nichevo net. Skin' yeshchyo raz.

lines.english: I sent the photo. Got it?

lessons.tip: Chat verbs come in pairs, but you can start with the short ones: отправить (to send), получить (to receive). Скинь is the casual "send me" (to one friend): Скинь фото!

lessons.title: Texting shorthand

sentences.english: By the way, where are you?
Please, I'll send the photo in a sec.

lines.english: Nothing much, watching a film. And you?
Dunno. Wanna go to the cinema?

lessons.tip: Russian texting is spelled the way people speak, with the vowels thrown out: спасибо → спс, пожалуйста → пжлст, наверное → мб. Fine with friends. Never in a message to your boss.

lessons.title: Social media

sentences.english: I want to subscribe to the channel.

sentences.target: Он смотрит видео и пишет комментарий.
sentences.english: He's watching a video and writing a comment.
sentences.translit: On smotrit video i pishet kommentariy.

sentences.english: She has a lot of followers.

fills.english: I want to subscribe to the channel.
I want to share the video.

lines.english: Did you see my new post?
Want to subscribe to my channel?

lessons.tip: Borrowed verbs get -овать in Russian: лайк becomes лайкать in chat talk, пост becomes постить. If you know the English word, you can usually guess the verb.

lessons.title: Emotions

sentences.english: At home it's boredom and loneliness.

sentences.target: Это моя гордость и моя радость.
sentences.english: This is my pride and my joy.
sentences.translit: Eto moya gordost' i moya radost'.

fills.english: I'm stressed and have no time.
At home it's boredom and loneliness.

lessons.tip: Abstract nouns ending in -ость (радость, гордость) and -ь in general (грусть, сеть) are feminine. Words like счастье and одиночество end in -е/-о and are neuter.

lessons.title: Feeling adjectives

sentences.target: Он злой, потому что он голодный.
sentences.translit: On zloy, potomu shto on golodnyy.

sentences.english: He's tired, it's time for him to sleep.
I'm in love and very happy.

fills.english: He's hungry, he wants to eat.
He's tired, it's time for him to sleep.
He's in love, but she isn't.

lessons.tip: Short forms of adjectives sit after "I am" and change by gender: он рад / она рада, он счастлив / она счастлива. Long forms (грустный, злой) sit before a noun or after "is" for general states.

lessons.title: How do you feel?

sentences.english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.

sentences.target: Я тебя понимаю, мне тебя жаль.
sentences.english: I understand you, I feel sorry for you.
sentences.translit: Ya tebya ponimayu, mne tebya zhal'.

sentences.english: Hang in there! I want to hug you.

fills.english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
I feel worse, I have a temperature.

lines.target: Мне хуже. У меня болит голова.
lines.translit: Mne khuzhe. U menya bolit golova.

lines.english: Don't worry! You need to rest.

lessons.tip: "I feel" = я чувствую себя + adverb: хорошо, плохо, лучше. Не + imperative is the friendly "don't…": не волнуйся (don't worry), не расстраивайся (don't be upset).

lessons.title: Relationships

sentences.target: У них ссора, но они хотят помириться.
sentences.english: They had an argument, but they want to make up.
sentences.translit: U nikh ssora, no oni khotyat pomirit'sya.

sentences.english: I believe you and I trust you.

lessons.tip: Verbs about people take the accusative of a pronoun, not the dative: я тебя люблю (I love you), я его знаю. Меня→тебя→его→её→нас→вас→их. Don't mix them up: мне нравится (dative) but я тебя люблю (accusative).

lessons.title: Compliments

sentences.english: Thank you very much! You're welcome.
It's interesting with you, I'm pleased.

fills.english: Thank you very much! — You're welcome.

lines.target: Не за что. Ты мне нравишься.
lines.translit: Ne za shto. Ty mne nravish'sya.

lessons.tip: A compliment is just ты + adjective: ты красивая, ты классный. Adjectives change for gender: красивый (he) / красивая (she). Add очень for extra warmth.

lessons.title: Getting to know you

sentences.target: Вы давно здесь? Нет, я здесь первый раз.
sentences.english: Have you been here long? No, it's my first time here.
sentences.translit: Vy davno zdes'? Net, ya zdes' pervyy raz.

sentences.english: Let's get acquainted! Nice to meet you.
How do you like the city? Did you like it?

fills.english: Where are you from? I'm from England.

lines.target: Я из России. Вы надолго здесь?
lines.english: I'm from Russia. Are you here for long?
lines.translit: Ya iz Rossii. Vy nadolgo zdes'?

lessons.tip: ты is for friends, вы is for strangers, older people and groups. With вы the verb ends in -те or -ете: Где вы работаете? Откуда вы? When in doubt with someone you've just met, use вы.

lessons.title: Politeness

items.english: be so kind / excuse me, could you

sentences.english: Could I have the bill, please.
I beg your pardon, I'm late.
Huge thanks! All the best, good luck!

fills.english: Could I have the bill, please.

lessons.tip: Polite Russian is made of soft openers: будьте добры (be so kind) + request, разрешите / позвольте (allow me) + verb. They sound formal on purpose, and people notice when you use them.

lessons.title: Topics

sentences.target: Я не люблю политику и экономику.
sentences.english: I don't like politics and the economy.
sentences.translit: Ya ne lyublyu politiku i ekonomiku.

sentences.target: Вчера был футбольный матч, а потом сериал.
sentences.english: Yesterday there was a football match, and then a series.
sentences.translit: Vchera byl futbol'nyy match, a potom serial.

sentences.english: It's a secret, not a joke.

fills.english: It's not a joke, it's a secret.
Yesterday there was a football match.

lines.target: Нормально. Много работы. А у тебя?
lines.english: Fine. Lots of work. And you?
lines.translit: Normal'no. Mnogo raboty. A u tebya?

lines.target: Тоже. Ты смотрел вчера футбольный матч?
lines.english: Same. Did you watch the football match yesterday?
lines.translit: Tozhe. Ty smotrel vchera futbol'nyy match?

lessons.tip: To talk about a topic use о + the prepositional: о чём? (about what?), о политике. For asking, learn the chunks: Какие новости? Как дела? О чём фильм? Don't worry about case endings yet.

lessons.title: Reactions

sentences.target: Ничего себе, у тебя три машины?
sentences.translit: Nichevo sebe, u tebya tri mashiny?

sentences.english: What a pity, but it happens.

fills.english: He lost his key. — What a pity!

lines.english: Yes, a red one. And cheap!

lessons.tip: Russians use short exclamations to show they're listening: Серьёзно? Да ну! Ничего себе! You don't need grammar, just tone. Say them with rising or falling voice depending on the surprise.

lessons.title: Saying goodbye

items.english: glad to have met you (man speaking)

sentences.english: I have to go, it was nice.
Have a nice day! Have a good evening!
Have a good weekend, we'll talk!

sentences.target: Береги себя, передавай привет маме, до встречи!
sentences.english: Take care, say hi to your mum, see you!
sentences.translit: Beregi sebya, peredavay privet mame, do vstrechi!

fills.english: It's time for me to go.

lines.english: I have to go. It was nice!

lessons.tip: Goodbyes are polite wishes in the genitive: приятного дня, хорошего вечера, хороших выходных. Learn each as one block. Мне пора = I have to go: the best exit line in Russian.
